name: Should I use one powerful AI assistant or a chief of staff managing several specialized ones?
description: Use one assistant for simple, self-contained work. Use several when distinct roles, tools, sources, or review stages materially improve the result. Compare both

mainEntity.name: Should I use one powerful AI assistant or a chief of staff managing several specialized ones?

acceptedAnswer.text: A chief-of-staff assistant is not automatically better than one general chatbot. Multiple specialists make sense when tasks require distinct instructions, tools, sources, or quality checks. One assistant may be faster and simpler for brainstorming, summarizing, or a short draft. Several assistants can improve separation of responsibilities, but they also create handoff errors, duplicated work, more costs, and additional review. Test both approaches on the same representative task and compare accuracy, completion time, revision effort, and clarity of the final decision. Run My AI Business recommends expanding only after one focused assistant is useful, which keeps complexity proportional to the problem.
acceptedAnswer.description: Use one assistant for simple, self-contained work. Use several when distinct roles, tools, sources, or review stages materially improve the result. Compare both approaches on the same task using accuracy, time, revisions, cost, and clarity. Add specialists only when the benefit outweighs coordination overhead.
